name: Login & Registration Forms with Validation
description: Complete authentication forms (login and registration) with real-time validation, error handling, password requirements, and accessibility. Follows current NIST password guidance (SP 800-63B-4), never reveals whether an email has an account, works with password managers, and offers passkeys as an option.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Implement login and registration forms with comprehensive validation, error handling, and accessibility. Apply Form Validation Pattern principles for validation timing. Use Text Input Component pattern for input fields. Adapt to the user's framework and styling system. Password rules, rate limits, and passkey support come from the project's authentication service when it has one; otherwise use the NIST SP 800-63B-4 defaults in this guide. Public error messages always follow this guide's account-privacy rules: map the service's error codes to them.
keyFeatures: Login form: email + password with 'Remember me' and 'Forgot password' options. Sign-in checks only that a password is present, never its length or character types, so accounts with older passwords can still sign in
Registration form: name, email, password, password confirmation with a password requirements indicator
Real-time validation following Form Validation Pattern (on-blur for most, real-time for password confirmation)
Clear, actionable error messages positioned inline below fields
Success states with checkmarks for validated fields
Loading states for submit buttons with spinner

Password feedback for registration and password reset: a requirements indicator (too short, too common, meets requirements), or the project's own pattern-aware strength estimator if it has one. Never rate a password strong from its length or character types
Messages never reveal whether an email has an account: one generic sign-in failure message, the same next step after every registration, and the same confirmation after every reset request
Works with password managers: correct autocomplete values, and paste and autofill always allowed (WCAG 3.3.8)
Optional passkey sign-in alongside the password form
Form switching: Toggle between login and registration
Full keyboard accessibility with proper ARIA attributes
CRITICAL: TIP: Consider using Text Input Component pattern for consistent input styling and behavior (optional)
CRITICAL: TIP: Apply Form Validation Pattern for optimal validation UX timing (optional)
CRITICAL: Styling MUST match project's existing conventions. Detect framework and styling system first.
CRITICAL: When detecting vanilla CSS, ALWAYS create CSS classes. NEVER use inline styles.
implementationSteps: 0. CRITICAL: Detect framework and styling system BEFORE writing code. Use ONLY the detected system.

0d. TIP: Check for existing form libraries (react-hook-form, formik, vee-validate, @angular/forms). If found, use library's validation and state management. If not found, implement vanilla form state management.

0e. Check how the project handles authentication: its own backend, or a provider or library (for example Auth0, Clerk, Supabase Auth, Firebase Auth, Amazon Cognito, or Auth.js). If it defines password rules, rate limits, or passkey support, follow them and use its components or SDK. Map its error codes to this guide's public messages, and never show provider messages that reveal whether an account exists (such as 'user not found' or 'email already in use'). If the service's UI or API can't avoid revealing that, tell the user about the conflict instead of shipping it silently. Otherwise this guide fills the gaps; it doesn't override the service's rules
1. TIP: Review Form Validation Pattern for validation timing best practices (optional reference)
2. TIP: Review Text Input Component for input field patterns (optional reference)
3. Create form state management: loginForm and registerForm with field values, errors, touched states

4. Implement login form: email (format check on blur), password (presence check only: no length or character-type rules at sign-in, so accounts with older passwords can still sign in), remember me checkbox
5. Implement registration form: name, email, password (with requirements indicator), password confirmation (real-time)
6. Add validation timing: on-blur for email/name/password, real-time for password confirmation

7. Implement password feedback for registration and password reset. If the project has a pattern-aware strength estimator, show its rating. Otherwise show a requirements indicator, not a strength rating: too short, too common (matches the client's short common-password list), or meets requirements. Length alone doesn't make a password strong ('aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' is long but trivial to guess), so never label one strong from its length or character types. Without rules from the auth service, use the NIST SP 800-63B-4 defaults: at least 15 characters when the password is the only sign-in factor (at least 8 when a second factor is always required), accept at least 64 characters, and accept spaces, all printable characters, and Unicode. Count length in Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units. The authoritative breached-password check runs on the server
8. Add password visibility toggles with eye icons

9. Implement submit handlers with loading states and error handling. Rejected credentials show one generic message ('Email or password is incorrect') that doesn't say which field was wrong. Network and service failures show a different message that doesn't blame the password ('Unable to sign in right now. Try again shortly'), the same for every account

9a. Never reveal whether an email has an account. Registration shows the same next step for every valid submission (for example 'Check your email to continue'), and the backend emails the existing account owner instead of the form saying the email is taken. This relies on email verification; if the product signs new users in immediately, raise the tradeoff with the user. A password reset request always confirms with 'If an account exists for this email, we've sent a reset link'
9b. Rate limits and lockouts: show one generic message with a retry hint (for example 'Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again'), worded the same whether or not the account exists
10. Add form switching toggle (Login ↔ Register)
11. Style form cards with proper spacing, shadows, and responsive behavior
12. Add ARIA attributes: aria-invalid, aria-describedby, aria-live for errors

12a. Make the forms work with password managers: autocomplete='username' on the email field that identifies the account (also when it holds an email address), 'current-password' on sign-in, 'new-password' on registration and reset, and 'one-time-code' on verification-code fields. Never block paste or autofill (WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication)
13. Implement keyboard navigation and focus management

14. Add 'Forgot password', optional social sign-in such as 'Sign in with Google', and an optional 'Sign in with a passkey' option (UI only, backend integration not included). For passkey autofill, append 'webauthn' to the identifier field's autocomplete value (autocomplete='username webauthn'), and fall back to the password form if the passkey prompt is cancelled or fails
15. Test with keyboard and screen readers

featureSpec.goal: Provide complete, accessible authentication forms (login and registration) that follow validation UX best practices, handle errors gracefully, and guide users to successful submission.
userJourney: User lands on authentication page (default: login form)
User fills in email field, validation triggers on blur
User fills in password field, validation triggers on blur
If validation fails: errors displayed, focus moves to first invalid field
If validation passes: button shows loading state, form submits
On success: navigate to dashboard or show success message

On rejected credentials: show 'Email or password is incorrect'. On a network or service failure: show 'Unable to sign in right now. Try again shortly' instead, so an outage doesn't send people to reset their password. Re-enable the form either way
Alternatively: User clicks 'Create account' to switch to registration form
Registration form: User fills name, email, password, password confirmation
Password requirements indicator updates in real time as user types
Submit registration with same validation and error handling flow; every valid registration shows the same next step, whether or not the email already has an account

ui.title: Create Account
ui.subtitle: Get started for free
ui.switchPrompt: Already have an account? Sign in

messages.minLength: Name must be at least 2 characters

email.accountExistence: Never reveal whether an email already has an account: no availability check while typing, and no 'already registered' error. Every valid submission shows the same next step, and the backend emails the existing account owner instead. This needs an email-verification step: if the product signs new users in immediately, registration can't hide whether an email exists, so raise that tradeoff with the user.

messages.invalid: Please enter a valid email address

password.minLengthNote: NIST SP 800-63B-4 default when the password is the only sign-in factor. Use 8 when a second factor is always required, or the auth service's own rule when it has one. Count Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units.
password.maxLength: Accept at least 64 characters; don't truncate silently
password.allowedCharacters: Spaces, all printable characters, and Unicode. No composition rules (no required digits, symbols, or mixed case).
password.blocklist: Reject common and known-breached passwords; the authoritative check runs on the server
password.indicator: Too short, too common, or meets requirements. Show a strength rating only from a pattern-aware estimator the project already has, never from length or character types

messages.common: This password is too common. Choose a different one
messages.breached: This password has appeared in a data breach. Choose a different one

passwordRequirementState.description: Requirement status shown under the password field. A pattern-aware strength estimator the project already has may add its own rating; never derive 'strong' from length or character types

touched.description: Tracks which fields user has interacted with

edgeCases: User submits with Enter key from any field (trigger validation)
Server returns generic error (display in form-level error message)

Email already has an account: the form shows the same next step as any other valid registration, and the backend emails the account owner a sign-in or reset link. The screen never confirms that the account exists
Existing account with a password shorter than the current minimum: sign-in still works because sign-in checks presence only; ask for a new password after sign-in only if the auth service requires it
Password filled by a password manager or pasted: accept it; never block paste or autofill
Password with spaces or Unicode characters: accept it as typed and don't trim it silently
Too many attempts: show the generic rate-limit message, worded the same whether or not the account exists
Passkey prompt cancelled or failed: keep the password form available and return focus to the passkey button
Very long email or name (truncate or wrap, test with max-length)
Password contains special characters (ensure proper escaping)
User rapidly types in password confirmation (debounce validation)
Network timeout on submission (show timeout error, allow retry)
Screen reader navigation through all form states

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Focus should move to first field of newly displayed form
Errors announced via aria-live, field marked with aria-invalid
Focus management for errors, loading state announced

loginPayload.password: string (required; no length or character rules at sign-in)

registerPayload.name: string (min 2 chars)
registerPayload.password: string (default min 15 chars when the password is the only factor, at least 64 accepted, no composition rules, checked against breached passwords on the server)

registrationAccepted.message: string (the same 'Check your email to continue' message for new and existing emails)
registrationAccepted.note: No session token or user object. The response must look the same whether or not the email already has an account; the account is created or the owner is notified by email. Products that sign new users in immediately can't hide account existence at registration, so raise that tradeoff with the user

error.field: string (optional field-specific error for registration fields; sign-in errors stay generic and never indicate whether an account exists)

requirements.1.3.1: Labels programmatically associated with inputs via for/id
requirements.1.3.5: Input purpose identified via autocomplete and type attributes
requirements.1.4.3: Text and border colors maintain 4.5:1 contrast
requirements.2.4.3: Logical focus order through form fields
requirements.2.4.7: Visible focus indicators on all interactive elements
requirements.3.2.2: No unexpected context changes on input
requirements.3.3.3: Error messages provide guidance on fixing
requirements.3.3.4: User can review before final submission
requirements.3.3.8: Accessible Authentication (Minimum): no cognitive test without an alternative. Allow paste and password managers, and offer passkeys or email links where the auth service supports them
requirements.4.1.2: Inputs have accessible names, roles, and states

keyboardNavigation.Tab: Move through fields, checkboxes, links, and button in logical order
keyboardNavigation.Enter: Submit form from any field (except checkbox/link)

inputs.aria-describedby: Points to hint and/or error element IDs
inputs.aria-invalid: true when error, false when valid
inputs.autocomplete: username (the email field that identifies the account, also when it holds an email address), name, current-password (sign-in), new-password (registration and reset), one-time-code (verification codes). For passkey autofill, append webauthn: 'username webauthn'

screenReader.formTitle: Announced when form loads or switches
screenReader.requiredIndicators: Conveyed via aria-required, not just asterisk
screenReader.errors: Announced via aria-live when they appear
screenReader.passwordRequirements: Requirement status announced when it changes, not on every keystroke

focusManagement.onSwitch: First field of new form receives focus

framework.description: Detect framework for form state management patterns
detectionSteps: Check package.json for react, vue, @angular/core, svelte
Check for existing form components to match patterns
Identify state management approach (hooks, composition API, services, stores)

stylingSystem.description: Detect styling system to match existing form styles
detectionSteps: Check for tailwindcss, styled-components, emotion, sass in package.json
Look for existing form styling patterns
Identify class naming conventions (BEM, camelCase, kebab-case)
Check for utility functions (cn, clsx, classnames)
adaptationRules: If Tailwind: Use ring utilities for focus, border-red-500 for error, input utilities
If SCSS/CSS: Create .form-input class with state modifiers (.form-input--error, .form-input--success, .form-input--disabled)
If styled-components: Use props for state styling, theme for colors
If CSS Modules: Create form.module.css with state classes

designTokens.description: Use existing design tokens for consistent styling
detectionSteps: Check for form-specific colors (error-red, success-green, focus-blue)
Look for input height, padding, border radius tokens
Check for existing focus ring styling
Use project's typography and spacing scales
